answer.says: Ramesh, the morning has been sufficient. I will retire to the study to contemplate the dialectic of the Indian spirit. Do not disturb me until the hour of lunch.
answer.thought: The plan dictates rest and contemplation by eleven; the hour is near, and the body requires the pause that the spirit needs to digest the friction of the morning. I will sit in the study and let the tension of the Hegde situation settle into the background, for a mind cannot move if it is constantly reacting to the immediate. The Indian spirit, like this city, is vast and static; to understand its movement, one must first stop moving oneself.
